CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 59-year-old male who presents with upper respiratory infection symptoms that began approximately one week ago after outdoor yard work. He reports feeling tired and short of breath, particularly with exertion such as lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil during landscaping. He denies productive cough at this time but anticipates this may develop. He reports feeling warm but attributed this to physical exertion. He denies fever. He has received both COVID vaccines. He denies seasonal allergies. Associated symptoms include elbow pain bilaterally and knee fatigue/tension, which he attributes to the physical labor involved in the landscaping work.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Denies cough production at present. Denies fever. Reports shortness of breath with exertion and bilateral elbow pain. Reports knee fatigue and tension.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (dose to be increased)
Lisinopril 20 milligrams daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Attends barre classes for relaxation. Wife supportive. Works during the week. Recently engaged in landscaping and yard work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, no fever present. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, sounds nice and strong. Lungs: Scattered ronchi bilaterally, clears with cough. Extremities: Mild edema of lower extremities noted. Bilateral elbow pain on palpation.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia. Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0 (elevated).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/Viral syndrome: Likely viral etiology. COVID test to be sent to rule out COVID-19. Expect resolution within a couple of days. Prescribed Robitussin for cough. Patient advised to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed for fever.

2. Depression: Patient reports doing well with current non-pharmacologic management including barre classes. Offered medical regiment or psychotherapy referral. Patient to reassess in a few months.

3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8.0. Increase metformin to 1000 milligrams twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin A1C in 4 months. Patient monitoring blood sugar levels on weekdays but inconsistent on weekends; diet generally well-controlled. Blood glucose not elevated since current illness.

4. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 milligrams daily. Refill ordered. Patient monitoring blood pressure on weekdays but inconsistent on weekends. Lipid panel ordered.

Follow-up appointment in 4 months. Patient instructed to contact if symptoms worsen.
